title: Economic Woes Drag Down Trump's Ratings as Voters Head to Midterm Polls
snippet: With persistent inflation and high cost-of-living concerns front of mind, President Donald Trump faces record-low economic approval numbers, posing a major hurdle for Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections.
content:
As American voters prepare to cast their ballots in this week's midterm elections, President Donald Trump faces a challenging political landscape driven by deep public dissatisfaction over the state of the economy. Latest polling figures show Trump’s economic approval ratings hovering near second-term lows, with persistent inflation and high cost-of-living concerns creating significant headwinds for the Republican Party.

Surveys across the board highlight a stark reality for the administration: voters' frustration with prices is actively dragging down the president's overall standing. According to recent poll averages tracked by forecaster Nate Silver, a staggering 69.5% of voters disapprove of Trump's handling of inflation, compared to just 25.3% who approve. RealClearPolitics aggregations paint a similarly grim picture, reflecting a 70.4% disapproval rating on price levels—an issue consistently cited by Americans as their primary concern.

Dissatisfaction Reaches Trump’s Base

The economic anxiety is no longer confined to political independents or Democrats. A fresh NBC News poll released Sunday revealed that 53% of self-identified Republicans are dissatisfied with current economic conditions. Overall, three out of four respondents expressed discontent with the economy, with half calling for substantial structural changes.

Even core Trump supporters are expressing frustration. Data from a recent Politico survey indicates that 54% of Trump voters view the rising cost of living as their top priority, with many pointing to administration policies—specifically tariffs and foreign conflicts—as contributing factors to elevated gas prices and broader price spikes.

Democrats Gain Edge on Traditional GOP Strengths

The economic headwinds have allowed Democrats to pull ahead on key financial questions that traditionally favored Republicans. A Focaldata-Financial Times poll showed 47% of voters trusting Democrats to handle inflation compared to 34% for Republicans. Furthermore, despite Trump’s repeated emphasis on his signature tax cuts, a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll found Democrats holding a seven-point advantage on the issue of taxation.

For his part, President Trump has pushed back against the polling data, dismissing negative reports as unrepresentative during recent campaign rallies in South Carolina and Mississippi while forecasting strong midterm victories for his party based on what he characterizes as a robust economy.

However, with approval numbers on trade, taxes, and inflation dropping to annual lows in recent Harvard CAPS/Harris polling, pollsters and analysts note that economic sentiment could prove to be the decisive factor when voters make their voices heard on Tuesday.
